To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The thermal expansion coefficient of MnCo2−xCuxO4 spinel oxides decreases with Cu content and the electrical conductivity increases.
Fe and Cu substitution in the MnCo2O 4 spinel affects the crystal structure, electrical conductivity and thermal expansion of the materials.

(1) the addition of 0.5 mol.% Fe to MnCo2O₄ decreases its electrical conductivity by 2 orders of magnitude and its thermal expansion coefficient (T.E.C) by 20%, (2) the addition of Cu to MnCo2−xCuxO4 increases its electrical conductivity by up to a factor of 3 and (3) the addition of Fe and Cu to MnCoO₄ has no significant effect on its phase stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new class of spinels with the general formula MnCo2−xCuxO4 (x=0, 0.1, and 0.3).

the synthesis and characterization of the thermal and electrical properties of Fe and Cu substituted MnCo2O 4 spinel oxides, which are potential coating materials for solid oxide fuel cell interconnects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe doping is beneficial for both the electrical conductivity and TEC, while the Cu doping is beneficial for the electrical conductivity, but not for the TEC.
the thermal expansion and electrical properties of MnCo2O 4 spinels can be modified by Fe and Cu substitution.
the Fe doped MnCo1.9Fe0.1O4 spinel oxide is the most promising coating material for SOFC interconnects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fe doping is more effective at reducing the TEC of the spinel oxides than Cu.
the thermal expansion and electrical properties of the spinel oxide coatings can be tailored for a specific application by choosing an appropriate composition.
the TEC of spinel oxides can be tailored to match that of ferritic stainless steels by adjusting the Fe and Cu content.
